title: Tesla Opens Cybercab Orders at $29,990 — But the $299 Monthly Catch Is Brutal
summary: Tesla Cybercab now on sale for $29,990 with a mandatory $299/month autonomy subscription. Geofence-locked, no steering wheel. Here's what builders need to know about the fine print.

# Tesla Opens Cybercab Orders at $29,990 — But the $299 Monthly Catch Is Brutal


By OpenTools Team


·


November 15, 2026


Tesla has opened Cybercab orders to select customers at $29,990, with mandatory $299/month autonomy subscriptions. The fine print reveals the two‑seater is geofence‑locked, Tesla can change pricing with one month's notice, and the car becomes useless without the active subscription.


## $29,990 to Buy, $299/Month to Actually Drive


Tesla has officially opened orders for the Cybercab to select customers, pricing the two-seat autonomous vehicle at **$29,990** with deliveries estimated for December 2026,[TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/14/tesla-opens-cybercab-pre-orders-for-personal-use-with-geo-restrictions-and-a-299-monthly-fee/) reported Friday. But the headline price hides the real cost: a mandatory **$299/month Autonomy Subscription** that, if cancelled, renders the vehicle immobile.


The subscription agreement, reviewed by[Electrek](https://electrek.co/2026/11/14/tesla-cybercab-autonomy-subscription-agreement-terms/) , states bluntly: "Your Cybercab will not operate without an active Autonomy Subscription." Since the vehicle has no steering wheel or pedals, there is no manual fallback. Stop paying, and you own a $30,000 sculpture in your garage. The agreement also gives Tesla the right to **change the subscription price with one month's notice** — no rate lock, no cap.


## The Fine Print Tesla Doesn't Put in the Ad


[Electrek](https://electrek.co/2026/11/14/tesla-cybercab-autonomy-subscription-agreement-terms/) 's analysis of the Autonomy Subscription Agreement v20261112 reveals terms that turn ownership into something closer to a conditional rental. Beyond the price-change clause, Tesla can remotely access, locate, restrict, or control the vehicle at any time, and can end your access entirely — with no remedies for the owner beyond what's in the terms. The agreement also states Tesla does not prorate the monthly fee if it suspends service, such as after three "strikeouts" for improper or unsafe use, per the agreement text published by[Electrek](https://electrek.co/2026/11/14/tesla-cybercab-autonomy-subscription-agreement-terms/) .


The cabin camera collects "Autonomy Data" including image data from above the rear-view mirror, retained for 30 days by default, according to the same[Electrek](https://electrek.co/2026/11/14/tesla-cybercab-autonomy-subscription-agreement-terms/) review. Modifications — wraps, tint, wheel changes — are banned unless done through Tesla or an authorized provider, with violations triggering subscription suspension. As X user Mark Valorian described it: "an endless variable-rate lease with a ridiculous down payment."


## Geofence-Locked: Only Works Where Tesla Says


The Cybercab only operates inside "Tesla-enabled Robotaxi geofences," and Tesla can "expand, reduce, relocate, or otherwise modify the operating area at any time" — even after purchase.[TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/14/tesla-opens-cybercab-pre-orders-for-personal-use-with-geo-restrictions-and-a-299-monthly-fee/) notes that delivery must be accepted in a handful of Texas cities. Buyers also must pay a **$1,000 nonrefundable deposit** .


The geofencing has already drawn scrutiny.[Electrek](https://electrek.co/2026/11/14/tesla-cybercab-autonomy-subscription-agreement-terms/) tested actual coverage areas and found they cover only 59% to 78% of advertised maps. Parts of the Houston map have been called "fake" by the person tracking service areas. Tesla AI chief Ashok Elluswamy confirmed the Cybercab will operate unsupervised inside the same geo locations as the company's Robotaxi fleet, serving only the owner's needs — not available for commercial ride-hailing.


## Musk Himself Says the Price Is Too High


In a rare moment of a CEO criticizing his own company's pricing, Musk posted on X that the $299 monthly fee "is too high" and suggested it "should match the cost of Tesla Full Self-Driving and connectivity for other models, which is more like ~$115/month," per[TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/14/tesla-opens-cybercab-pre-orders-for-personal-use-with-geo-restrictions-and-a-299-monthly-fee/) . Musk also said the Cybercab "will be available nationwide, as we receive regulatory approval."


This pricing gap is especially galling for existing Tesla owners who bought Full Self-Driving capability — some paid up to $15,000 — and were promised eventual autonomy. In early 2026, Tesla stopped outright FSD sales and moved to a $99/month subscription that still requires full-time driver supervision. Those owners now watch Tesla sell a new vehicle with unsupervised autonomy for triple the monthly subscription, running on the same AI4 hardware already in their cars, per[Electrek](https://electrek.co/2026/11/14/tesla-cybercab-autonomy-subscription-agreement-terms/) .


## Personal Use Only — No Uber, No Fleet Income


The autonomy agreement explicitly bans commercial use: owners cannot put their Cybercab on Tesla's Robotaxi network, Uber, any delivery app, or a rental platform without Tesla's written authorization. This directly contradicts Musk's earlier promise that owners could "add it to the fleet and make money while they sleep."


The total cost over 5 years, assuming 59 paid months at $299, comes to roughly **$47,631** before insurance, registration, charging, or taxes, per[Electrek](https://electrek.co/2026/11/14/tesla-cybercab-autonomy-subscription-agreement-terms/) 's calculations. Meanwhile, Tesla has announced it will end Cybertruck production in 2027 to free up factory capacity for more Cybercabs,[TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/14/tesla-opens-cybercab-pre-orders-for-personal-use-with-geo-restrictions-and-a-299-monthly-fee/) reports — signaling that the company sees Cybercab, not Cybertruck, as its future manufacturing priority.


## What This Means for Autonomous Vehicle Builders


The Cybercab's rollout is both a milestone and a warning for developers in the autonomous vehicle space. On one hand, a sub-$30,000 autonomous EV shipping to consumers has no parallel in the industry — no competitor has come close to this price point. On the other, the mandatory subscription model and geofence restrictions preview a future where autonomous vehicles are never truly "owned" in the traditional sense.


For developers building on Tesla's platform or competing in the robotaxi space, the Cybercab's terms set a precedent: the hardware is a loss leader, the recurring software subscription is the real product. The Model Y runs the same AI4 computer and unsupervised FSD already operates in the same geofences — yet existing owners get nothing. Tesla's strategy is clear: a clean-slate revenue stream with $30,000 entry fees and locked-in subscriptions, free from obligations to legacy FSD buyers. Builders betting on Tesla's autonomy platform should price in the subscription model from day one.
